title: Flattening Every Memory Peak in Long-Context Mixture-of-Experts Training
notion_title: Bounding the memory bottlenecks of large mixture-of-experts training
authors: Shrey Pandit, Xuan-Phi Nguyen (equal contribution), Yiran Zhao, Shafiq Joty

code.title: LLEP code
code.label: no code for this paper; LLEP's code
code.note: no code is released for this paper's four operators or for the MoP stack (checked 3 October 2026); this is the authors' earlier Least-Loaded Expert Parallelism, Apache-2.0, whose assignment plan the dispatch replay on this page ports (about 20 minutes for the README and the plan function)

takeaway: Bounds the four main memory bottlenecks of large-MoE training inside a fixed GPU memory budget by scheduling rather than by approximating the computation, across expert dispatch, vocabulary projection, activation checkpointing and optimiser state.

headline.k: expert dispatch against LLEP, 65,536 tokens per rank, top-8
headline.d: at 1.01 to 1.10 times LLEP's speed, forward pass

headline.k: vocabulary projection, 32,768 tokens per GPU, V = 200,000
headline.d: 79.5 to 10.6 GiB for 4.4% more time, exact loss

headline.k: 120B, 241B and 667B MoE models on 16 to 64 H200s
headline.d: 8 to 32 times the reach of a tuned FSDP2 baseline

resources.by: Nguyen, Pandit, Xu, Xiong, Joty, arXiv 2601.17111
resources.n: the authors' earlier paper that PipelinedLLEP extends: reroute an overloaded expert's excess tokens, and its weights, to the least-loaded ranks.

resources.n: the rank layout the four operators are composed in; it already reports 4.7 to 8.2 times FSDP2's throughput and 1M-token context, which matters for reading this paper's end-to-end numbers.

resources.t: Cut Your Losses in Large-Vocabulary Language Models (Cut Cross-Entropy)
resources.n: the single-device fused cross-entropy that never forms the logit matrix; Ring-DTP is its multi-rank counterpart.
the three-scalar running maximum and sum that Ring-DTP folds strips into (Eq. 3), and that FlashAttention also rests on.

resources.by: Ren et al., USENIX ATC 2021, arXiv 2101.06840
resources.n: the CPU optimizer offload and AVX CPU Adam that OffloadStreamAdamW replaces as the update engine.
the clearest walkthrough of activation recomputation, ZeRO, context and expert parallelism, the components this paper schedules around (the relevant sections).

kb.n: 2019: the 16 bytes per parameter and the sharding of model state; the composed stack uses ZeRO-3 for dense weights, and OffloadStreamAdamW speeds up its offload descendant.
2019: vocabulary-parallel cross-entropy shards the output weight but needs the same batch on every rank; Ring-DTP keeps the shard and lets each rank keep its own batch.
2021: the expert-parallel MoE layer whose dispatch all-to-all and routing skew PipelinedLLEP bounds; Switch dropped overflow tokens with a capacity factor, this paper drops none.
2024: a top-2 sparse MoE trained at 32K context; the kind of model whose dispatch and logits this paper's bounds are about.
2024: the auxiliary-loss-free bias balancing used in this paper's end-to-end runs, and the fine-grained MoE shape (top-8 of many small experts) its benchmarks use.
2022: the same online-softmax trick applied to attention; Ring-DTP applies it to the vocabulary projection across ranks.
2023: another memory paper whose gain comes from when and where tensors live rather than from changing the arithmetic, at serving time.
2023: the approximate route (4-bit weights, paged 8-bit optimizer state) this paper deliberately excludes so its results stay comparable with full BF16 training.

topics.n: where this row is integrated; distributed training, memory and long-context training.
the row's second topic: sizing a run against the hardware you have.
the end-to-end models share Kimi K2's widths (hidden 7,168, 384 experts of width 2,048, top-8).
gpt-oss-20b, the model behind the SCO and optimizer benchmarks and the training-quality check.

verdict: Believe the mechanisms and the component memory numbers: the operators are exact by construction, and the checkpoint, optimizer-staging and projection numbers recompute from the configuration, as does Table 8 from our replay. Treat the end-to-end multiples as a result for the whole MoP stack against a weak FSDP2 baseline: single runs, no ablation of which operator buys what, and two printed multiples that contradict the text.
